paths.description: Public mobile homepage: entry point, content discovery, global navigation, preferences, performance and security.
New-games listing archetype, selected to test the main browse journey and form-factor routing.
Ranking/listing archetype, selected as a second high-value discovery route.
News/content route, selected to represent editorial content.
Primary conversion journey from the homepage to member registration/login.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical to the normal mobile screenshot and remains a hard-coded white/green surface; the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule or color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, icon and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference receives no adaptation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more capture is visually/byte identical to the default capture, and CSS inspection found no contrast preference handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations and preserve control boundaries and legible text.

findings.summary: Navigation swaps are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the homepage found no view-transition rules or API signal; representative links perform full, abrupt navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route/state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The mobile homepage is 2,882px tall, but the screenshot and CSS probe show static chrome with no progress indicator, shrinking header or scroll-state query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll-state-aware header or progress affordance where it helps orientation.

findings.summary: Core listing routes serve a desktop-only 950px layout into a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The new-games, ranking and news captures render the desktop www.mbga.jp layout as tiny scaled content at 360px; DOM evidence reports fixed 950px content and no viewport meta on the listing template.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep users on a responsive HTTPS route and replace fixed 950px desktop templates with intrinsic/fluid layouts and a valid viewport meta tag.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation do not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container usage; listing DOM uses fixed 720/740/950px widths, producing miniature desktop cards on narrow screens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries and intrinsic card grids so reused listings adapt to their available inline size.

findings.summary: Several footer targets are too short for touch.
findings.evidence: The active probe found five visible footer links only 15.39px high, well below a comfortable touch target, although keyboard outlines were visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive target boxes to at least 24px minimum and preferably about 44px without shrinking text.

findings.summary: The public member-registration journey dead-ends.
findings.evidence: The registration landing says 会員登録, but its only registration links resolve back to the same https://ssl.sp.mbga.jp/_reg URL and no form or next step exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a clear, functioning registration step or explain eligibility/availability and offer an actionable recovery route.

findings.summary: A generic system error appears without a recovery action.
findings.evidence: Every homepage capture shows システムエラーが発生しました in a transient toast, with no cause, retry, dismiss or next action.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the generic toast with contextual status and a retry/dismiss path; preserve the user’s location and input.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is slower than the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.8s (score 0.55), while the separate warm trace measured 1.40s; the throttled Lighthouse result indicates a meaningful slow-network risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, shorten render-blocking chains, and validate under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Caching, image delivery and render blocking waste load time.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 66 requests and 1,197,051 transferred bytes, including 1,038,487 image bytes and five parser-inserted blocking candidates; Lighthouse estimates 1,100KiB cache, 573KiB image and 1,060ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Set long immutable cache lifetimes on versioned assets, modernize image delivery, and defer/non-block non-critical scripts and styles.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 35KiB unused CSS and 42KiB unused JavaScript on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by surface and remove legacy or unused rules and script paths.

findings.summary: The document lacks a main landmark and includes unnamed image/link content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark; the active DOM probe found one image without alt and an empty visible anchor, while the image primitive found many hidden drawer images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark and ensure every meaningful image/control has an accessible name; use empty alt only for decoration.

findings.summary: Footer links fail minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured #0075ec on #d0d0d0 at 2.86:1 for 11px footer links, below WCAG’s 4.5:1 minimum.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker link color or lighter surface and retest all footer states.

findings.summary: The mobile viewport explicitly disables zoom.
findings.evidence: The live meta viewport contains maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails the meta-viewport accessibility audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and restrictive maximum-scale so users can zoom; ensure layouts reflow at magnification.

findings.summary: Important links are not crawlable and route templates are not mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found many javascript:void(0) links and the active probe counted 37; key game cards use onclick without href. Representative listing routes serve a desktop layout at 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation and maintain responsive canonical route templates.

findings.summary: Canonical and route signals downgrade to HTTP and disagree with the requested mobile URL.
findings.evidence: The new-games route redirected from https://sp.mbga.jp to http://www.mbga.jp and declares an http canonical; sitemap.xml fetch failed while robots.txt was available.
findings.suggestedFix: Use HTTPS canonicals, eliminate host/protocol downgrade redirects, and publish a reachable sitemap consistent with robots.

findings.summary: Share metadata is incomplete for a rich game portal.
findings.evidence: The probe found no JSON-LD and an empty og:description; the page represents games/news entities that could support accurate structured previews.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph descriptions and schema.org JSON-LD for the visible WebSite, games and editorial entities.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no CSP or HSTS. All four first-party cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; two are script-readable.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP and HSTS, mark HTTPS cookies Secure, use Lax/Strict where possible, and make sensitive cookies HttpOnly.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The main document lacks clickjacking protection, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy in addition to CSP/HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, nosniff, strict referrer policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Runtime routing is inconsistent across public surfaces.
findings.evidence: Home stays on sp.mbga.jp, but game/news/ranking routes redirect to a desktop www.mbga.jp template and registration moves to ssl.sp.mbga.jp, losing a consistent responsive context.
findings.suggestedFix: Unify routing and templates so navigation preserves device-appropriate state and HTTPS origin expectations.

findings.summary: The observed failure state is not actionable.
findings.evidence: A system-error toast appears during normal load with no retry, details, fallback content change or durable status; one analytics request also aborts in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide explicit retry/offline/error states and keep core content/actions usable when secondary requests fail.

findings.summary: Account creation is presented as available but cannot proceed.
findings.evidence: The account landing states normal registration is required, yet the registration control points back to the same page and exposes no next step.
findings.suggestedFix: Make account availability and requirements explicit and provide a reversible, functioning registration/login journey.

findings.summary: The image payload is disproportionate and uses legacy formats.
findings.evidence: Images account for 1,038,487 of 1,197,051 transferred bytes; 39 of 45 inspected images are PNG/GIF with no modern-format images, and 16 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert photographic/decorative assets to AVIF/WebP where suitable, consolidate sprites, provide responsive sources, and lazy-load below-fold images.

findings.summary: Decorative sprite and banner bytes dominate the mobile page.
findings.evidence: The five largest image resources alone transfer about 767KiB, mostly legacy @2x sprites; Lighthouse estimates 573KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an image/media budget and replace legacy oversized sprites with scoped SVG/modern raster assets loaded only where needed.
